terra.problem: The claim that the person who makes an evil plan is the one who pays for it overgeneralizes Haman’s fate. The passage does not promise that every evil scheme will rebound on its maker.
Saying Esther’s people were saved because she spoke implies their deliverance was complete here. Haman is executed in this passage, but the threat to the Jewish people has not yet been resolved.
Telling readers they do not have to fear anyone else’s scheme and that doing right will not be wasted suggests guarantees this passage does not make.
